place_fields.summary: A Shiva temple known for Vijayanagara-era architecture, carved pillars and a temple tank.

planning_attributes.description: Historic Shiva temple in Halasuru, Bengaluru, with ornate stone work, sculptural details, a Kalyani tank and a Kalyana Mantapa.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple is traditionally associated with the Vijayanagara period and Kempe Gowda-era Bengaluru; surviving inscriptions and architectural features reflect its historical development.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: In central Bengaluru on Ulsoor Road; Halasuru Metro station is nearby, and local buses, taxis and autos serve the area.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Temple hours can vary around rituals and festivals; visitors should follow temple instructions and remove footwear where required.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Modest dress and respectful conduct are appropriate; expect crowds during major Shiva festivals.
planning_attributes.notes: Regular visits are generally 30–60 minutes; parking around the busy central area may be limited.

place_fields.summary: A Shiva temple centered on a 65-foot seated Shiva statue, with a 32-foot Ganesha statue and symbolic pilgrimage attractions including Panch Dham and 12 Jyotirlinga displays.
place_fields.best_time: Early morning for a quieter visit; evening for the aarti/light-and-sound program

planning_attributes.description: Shivoham Shiva Temple is a modern Shiva shrine on Old HAL Airport Road, distinguished by its 65-foot meditative Shiva statue and additional devotional attractions.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Construction of the 65-foot Shiva idol began in 1994; the temple was inaugurated in February 1995 by the Shankaracharya of Sringeri. It was later renamed Shivoham Shiva Temple.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: On Old HAL Airport Road near Kemp Fort Mall; accessible by road via taxis, autos and BMTC buses. Indiranagar is a nearby Metro connection with a short road transfer.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: General darshan/show hours and special-entry arrangements can vary; verify current timings for tightly planned visits, especially during festivals.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Remove footwear where required, dress modestly, and follow crowd/temple instructions. Large festival crowds are possible.
planning_attributes.notes: The temple site is reported as open 24 hours, while regular darshan/show access has more limited hours; special activities may require booking.

place_fields.summary: A hilltop temple dedicated to Shanmukha (Murugan/Kartikeya), notable for its tall gopuram, six-faced deity imagery and distinctive crystal dome.

planning_attributes.description: Shrungagiri Sri Shanmukha Swami Temple is a hilltop shrine in the BEML area of Rajarajeshwari Nagar dedicated to Lord Shanmukha, also known as Murugan or Kartikeya.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: About 240 ft above ground level; the temple's gopuram is about 62 ft high.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple was built under the blessings and instructions of Sri Bharathi Theertha Mahaswamiji of Sringeri; its hilltop setting and architecture include a prominent gopuram and a large crystal dome.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: On BEML, Kempegowda Road in Rajarajeshwari Nagar; reachable by road, including via NICE Road, with local buses, taxis and autos.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Reported worship hours are split between morning and evening sessions; festival schedules can differ, so follow current temple notices.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The temple is on a hill and includes stairs; wear suitable footwear for the approach and follow temple customs.
planning_attributes.notes: The crystal dome is a major visual feature and the hilltop setting provides an elevated outlook over parts of Bengaluru.
